high.title: Kuo Ming-chien Resigns as Cathay United Bank Chairman; Cathay Financial to Appoint Him as Senior Advisor
high.summary:
Kuo Ming-chien has resigned from his roles as director of Cathay Financial Holdings, chairman and director of Cathay United Bank, and director of Cathay Private Equity. The resignation follows a conflict-of-interest controversy involving Cathay Securities Investment Trust (SITE). Kuo simultaneously served as a director at Cathay SITE and as an independent director at Alchip Technologies (世芯-KY), which made Alchip a related-party company of Cathay SITE. Despite this, Cathay SITE's discretionary accounts and eight funds proceeded to trade Alchip shares, triggering a NAV restatement and investor compensation process.

Total compensation amounts to approximately NT$490 million, covering roughly 50,500 beneficiaries across 47 distribution institutions, with a "best-case compensation" principle applied. Cathay SITE has also launched a broader review of all companies where Kuo held board or independent director roles during his tenure.

**Market Implications:** This is a significant corporate governance event for Cathay Financial Holdings (2882). Investor focus will be on regulatory scrutiny from the FSC, potential further penalties for Cathay SITE, and reputational risk for the broader Cathay group. The NT$490M compensation bill is manageable but signals deeper governance vulnerabilities. Watch for FSC follow-up actions and any impact on Cathay Financial's stock price and institutional investor sentiment.

high.title: Surprise: Qualcomm AI Transformation Makes UMC a Winner — Absence of TSMC Sparks Industry Debate
high.summary:
Qualcomm unveiled its largest-ever strategic transformation at its annual investor day on June 24, announcing a major push into the AI data center market. Among the first batch of 35 ecosystem partners disclosed, United Microelectronics Corp (UMC, 2303) was the sole foundry listed — with TSMC notably absent, sparking widespread industry discussion. Industry analysts interpret this as more than a standard foundry relationship, suggesting it may relate to integrated in-package power technology required for high-power AI chips. UMC's deep expertise in mature and specialty processes — combined with capabilities in power management ICs, on-wafer inductors, deep trench capacitors (DTC), and in-package power integration — positions it as a potentially high-value node in Qualcomm's AI data center supply chain. Qualcomm's press release directly quoted UMC CEO Jason Wang, who emphasized the growing importance of advanced packaging and manufacturing collaboration for next-generation data center performance and energy efficiency. Qualcomm also launched its "Dragonfly" product family, including the Dragonfly C1000 data center CPU and AI300 series.

**Market Implications:** This is a meaningful positive catalyst for UMC (2303), which has faced headwinds from sluggish mature-node demand. Inclusion as Qualcomm's sole foundry partner in an AI data center ecosystem could re-rate UMC's positioning in the AI supply chain narrative. Conversely, TSMC's absence from the list warrants monitoring — though it may reflect strategic confidentiality rather than exclusion. Fund managers should watch for follow-on order disclosures and UMC's capacity allocation announcements.

high.title: OpenAI's Self-Developed Chip "Jalapeño" Completes Design, Boosting Taiwan Supply Chain
high.summary: OpenAI has announced that its first self-developed AI chip, "Jalapeño," co-developed with Broadcom, has completed its design phase. Industry sources confirm that TSMC (2330) has been selected as the foundry for this chip, with volume production expected to ramp progressively. The chip is designed for AI inference workloads — delivering AI services to enterprise and consumer users — while large-scale training tasks continue to rely on other chip architectures. OpenAI's ultimate target is to deploy sufficient self-developed chips to consume 10GW of power globally, underscoring the extraordinary scale of planned investment.

high.title: Cathay Financial Holding Shareholder Tsai Chen-Yu Issues Statement Questioning Corporate Governance and FSC Oversight
high.summary: Cathay Financial Holding (2882) shareholder Tsai Chen-Yu — a member of the founding Lim Garden (霖園) Tsai family — issued his first formal public statement on June 25, escalating the ongoing controversy surrounding Cathay Securities Investment Trust's (國泰投信) related-party trading violations. Tsai questioned the fitness of Cathay United Bank (國泰世華銀行) Chairman Kuo Ming-chien, citing his concurrent board positions at Alchip Technologies (世芯-KY, 3661), Yung Ching (榮成, 1909), and two Hong Kong entities — Far East Horizon and Shuncheng Holdings — raising concerns about undisclosed capital structures and potential conflicts of interest. Tsai argues that overseeing a bank with over NT$5.4 trillion in assets and 10 million customers demands undivided attention. He further challenged the effectiveness of two independent directors — Wang Li-ling and Wu Tang-chieh, both former senior FSC officials — questioning whether regulatory familiarity may lead to lenient supervisory treatment. Tsai called on the FSC to conduct a thorough investigation into Cathay Financial's internal controls and corporate governance failures.

high.title: MediaTek Hits Limit-Down, IC Design Sector Suffers Heavy Selloff; Realtek and Novatek Also Plunge
high.summary:
Taiwan's stock market fell sharply on June 26, with the IC design sector bearing the brunt of the selloff. MediaTek (2454) triggered a limit-down circuit breaker at NT$3,880, while Realtek (2379) dropped 7.37% to NT$754 and Novatek (3034) fell 8.38% to NT$514. Market participants attributed the decline not to company-specific fundamental deterioration, but rather to profit-taking and deleveraging following a strong run-up fueled by AI ASIC, edge AI, Wi-Fi 7, product price hike, and consumer electronics recovery narratives. UBS maintained a constructive long-term view on MediaTek, citing product price increases, the Google TPU project, smartphone SoC demand, and emerging applications, raising its target price to NT$6,500 and projecting accelerating growth from Q4 onwards. However, UBS also flagged that MediaTek may implement broad price hikes of 5–10% from September due to rising advanced process, back-end packaging, and substrate costs. Realtek noted strong demand drivers in AI networking, Wi-Fi 7, automotive Ethernet, and high-speed switches, though router and broadband equipment adoption lagged expectations due to elevated memory costs. **Market implication:** The sharp correction in IC design leaders — particularly MediaTek hitting limit-down — signals elevated short-term volatility and deleveraging risk. Investors should monitor whether the selloff is contained or broadens into other technology sub-sectors.

---

high.title: Taiwan Stock Market Plunges Over 1,500 Points Intraday, Breaking 45K Level; Eight Major Electronic Blue-Chips Hammered — ASE Holds Firm in Green
high.summary:
Taiwan's equity market suffered a severe intraday selloff on June 26, with the TAIEX plunging over 1,500 points at its worst — breaching the psychologically critical 45,000-point level and touching a low of 44,667.72. The index opened at 46,188.6 before aggressive selling overwhelmed buyers. The selloff was triggered by a combination of Apple's 6%+ overnight decline on Wall Street, TSMC's ADR falling 1.32%, and a sharp 722-point drop in Taiwan futures during overnight trading — despite the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index surging 3.59% and Micron rallying 15.74% on strong earnings.

TSMC (2330) led the damage, opening at NT$2,360 and sliding to NT$2,340, single-handedly dragging the index down over 350 points and breaking its monthly moving average. MediaTek (2454) was another major casualty, hitting its limit-down price of NT$3,880 — a drop through the key NT$4,000 level — and accounting for approximately 190 points of index drag, though notable buy orders queued at the limit-down price. Delta Electronics (2308) fell over 8% to NT$1,815, contributing ~120 points of decline. Hon Hai (2317) showed relative resilience, with losses contained to ~2.5% and holding above the NT$250 support level. ASE Technology (3711) was the sole major electronic blue-chip to hold in positive territory.

**Market Implications:** This sharp correction reflects concentrated risk-off sentiment driven by Apple supply-chain concerns rather than broad semiconductor weakness. The divergence — strong Micron/Philadelphia Semi performance versus Apple-linked Taiwanese ODM/OEM names — suggests investors should differentiate between memory/AI semiconductor exposure and consumer electronics assembly exposure. TSMC's breach of its monthly moving average is a key technical development warranting close monitoring. MediaTek's limit-down move with buy orders queued may signal short-term overselling. Fund managers should assess whether this represents a buying opportunity in AI-linked names or the beginning of broader multiple compression.

high.title: Evergreen Marine Responds: Crew, Vessel, and Cargo Safe — Ship Clears Strait of Hormuz After Strike from Unidentified Projectile
high.summary:
Evergreen Marine (2603) confirmed that its Singapore-flagged vessel *Ever Lovely* was struck by an unidentified projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on June 25 at 21:55 Taipei time, approximately 3.6 nautical miles southeast of Khawr Naiwah on the Omani coast. The company reported that initial crew inspection found damage to the vessel's eaves and bridge windows, but that crew, ship, and cargo are all safe, with main engines and navigation systems fully operational and no seaworthiness concerns. The *Ever Lovely* has since safely exited the strait. Two additional Evergreen vessels — *Ever Unicorn* and *Ever Lotus* — have also cleared the Strait of Hormuz without incident. Evergreen now reports no vessels remain stranded within the Persian Gulf.

**Market Implications:** While the immediate crisis appears contained, the incident highlights ongoing geopolitical risk in one of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints. For investors in Evergreen Marine and the broader Taiwan shipping sector, near-term watch points include potential war-risk insurance premium increases, route diversion decisions, and freight rate impacts. Any escalation in Hormuz tensions could introduce material earnings risk for Taiwan's major carriers. The stock's reaction should be monitored given the market's already elevated volatility today.

high.title: Foreign Investors on Selling Spree — TSMC Breaks Below Monthly Moving Average, Testing NT$2,300; July Analyst Day to Update Outlook
high.summary: Foreign investors have aggressively sold TSMC (2330) for three consecutive trading sessions as of June 25, with net sells totaling approximately 47,280 thousand shares over that period. On June 26, TSMC's share price opened lower, broke below its monthly moving average (MA), and tested the NT$2,330 level intraday — briefly falling to NT$2,325, a level numerically below the stock's own ticker code (2330). The company's market capitalization consequently declined to approximately NT$60.55 trillion. Overall foreign investor net selling in the centralized market on June 25 reached NT$40.51 billion, with TSMC topping the sell list alongside Winbond (2337), PSMC (6770), Nanya Tech (2408), and Zhen Ding Tech (4958). Foreign futures net short positions also remain elevated at 81,051 contracts, though slightly reduced by 2,554 contracts. Market attention is now squarely focused on TSMC's July analyst day, where management is expected to update its demand and earnings outlook. The sustained foreign selling pressure, combined with a breach of the monthly MA, signals near-term technical deterioration. Fund managers should monitor whether TSMC can reclaim the monthly MA as a key support; failure to do so may extend broader index weakness given TSMC's outsized index weighting.

high.title: Taiwan Stock Market Plunges Over 1,000 Points Intraday — TSMC and Major Tech Stocks Under Pressure; ASE Leads Packaging Sector in Counter-Trend Resilience
high.summary: Taiwan's weighted index suffered an intraday decline of over 1,000 points on June 26, touching a low of 45,249 points, before recovering partially to 45,471 (down 783 points) as of the time of publication. The selloff was triggered by a combination of factors: U.S. May PCE inflation came in at 4.1% YoY (core PCE at 3.4%), rekindling expectations of further Fed rate hikes; weakness in major U.S. tech stocks including Apple (down 6.1% on product price increases tied to memory/storage costs), Nvidia, Microsoft, and Alphabet; and TSMC ADR falling 1.32% overnight, dragging Taiwan index futures down 722 points in the night session to 45,805. Foreign futures net short positions remain above 80,000 contracts, adding downward pressure on electronics heavyweights including TSMC (2330), MediaTek (2454), Delta Electronics (2308), and UMC (2303). Notably, ASE Technology Holding (3711) emerged as a bright spot, rising over 5% intraday to NT$674, leading the packaging and testing sub-sector against the broader market decline. The divergence between packaging/testing stocks and front-end semiconductor names is a key rotation signal worth monitoring. The elevated Fed rate hike expectations, combined with foreign selling and heavy futures short positioning, present a challenging near-term macro backdrop for Taiwan equities.

high.title: Wistron Board Immediately Approves USD 150M Capital Injection into California Subsidiary After Jensen Huang Praises US Factory Expansion
high.summary:
Wistron held a board meeting on June 26 and approved two major resolutions to expand capital expenditures in response to overseas factory construction and equipment procurement needs. The headline decision was a USD 150 million additional capital injection into its wholly-owned U.S. subsidiary, WisLab EMS Corporation, to support expanded operations in California. This move came just one day after NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, at NVIDIA's annual shareholder meeting on June 24, specifically named Wistron among supply chain partners actively building U.S.-based manufacturing capacity to support the AI ecosystem. The board also approved new domestic and overseas capex: TWD 1.7 billion for the Hsinchu plant, TWD 7.5 billion for the Kaohsiung plant, USD 24.5 million for Vietnam, and USD 22.7 million for Malaysia. Huang framed the AI data center's evolving role as shifting from pure compute provision toward a value-generating "AI Factory" model, underpinning the strategic rationale for Wistron's aggressive expansion. **Market implications:** This signals accelerating investment by Taiwan's EMS supply chain into U.S. AI infrastructure, driven by both NVIDIA demand and potential tariff/reshoring incentives. Investors in Wistron and related AI server supply chain names should take note of the significant multi-geography capex commitment, which may pressure near-term free cash flow but positions the company favorably for long-term AI server order growth.

---

high.title: Taiwan Stock Market Plunges 1,683 Points for Fourth Consecutive Decline — MediaTek Hits Limit-Down, TSMC Falls NT$50
high.summary: Taiwan's benchmark weighted index closed down 1,683.5 points (-3.64%) at 44,571.76 on June 26, marking its fourth consecutive session of losses and recording the third-largest point decline in closing history. TSMC (2330) fell NT$50 to NT$2,340 (-2.09%), breaking below its monthly moving average. MediaTek (2454) hit limit-down, breaching the NT$4,000 psychological level, while Delta Electronics (2308) plunged approximately 9%. Hon Hai (2317) dropped over 3%. The three stocks alone accounted for 815 index points of the decline. Total turnover reached a massive NT$1.549 trillion. The selloff was triggered by a combination of factors: rising U.S. rate-hike fears, elevated tech valuation concerns, and a broad Asian equity rout — South Korea's KOSPI fell over 8% intraday (triggering a circuit breaker) and the Nikkei dropped over 4.5%. First Securities Investment Advisory noted that U.S. May PCE inflation surged to 4.1%, reinforcing concerns over Federal Reserve policy tightening. **Market implication:** The broad-based breakdown across all short- and medium-term moving averages signals significant technical damage. Fund managers should reassess near-term exposure to Taiwan large-cap technology names, particularly those with stretched valuations.

high.title: Institutional Investors Net Sell NT$205.5 Billion — Foreign Investors Post Second-Largest Single-Day Net Sale in History; Weekly Record Broken
high.summary: Taiwan's three major institutional investors combined to net sell NT$205.527 billion on June 26, reflecting extreme risk-off sentiment. Foreign investors (excluding foreign prop desks) sold a net NT$143.189 billion — the second-largest single-day foreign net sale on record. Critically, this week alone saw foreign investors set both the all-time largest and second-largest daily net-sell records, representing an unprecedented two-day wave of foreign capital outflow. Proprietary dealers also sold heavily, with a combined net sell of NT$70.733 billion (self-directed: NT$16.119 billion; hedging desks: NT$54.6 billion). Investment trusts (投信) were the sole buyers, purchasing a net NT$8.395 billion. The TAIEX opened lower by 66.66 points at 46,188.6 before plunging intraday to 44,454.22 (-1,801 points), with 1,819 listed and OTC stocks declining versus only 165 advancing, and 37 stocks hitting limit-down. Late-session bargain buying in TSMC, UMC, Nanya Tech, and Winbond helped narrow losses. **Market implication:** The scale and velocity of foreign capital outflows is a critical warning signal for fund managers. The monthly moving average support has been lost; continued foreign selling next week could test deeper technical levels. Monitor whether foreign selling accelerates or stabilizes as a key sentiment indicator.

high.title: Taiwan Stock Market Plunges 1,700 Points — Retail Investor FOMO Backfires; Institutions Urge Caution
high.summary:
Taiwan's equity market suffered a sharp "Black Friday" selloff on June 26, with the TAIEX plunging as much as 1,775 points intraday to 44,480, breaching both the 45,000-point threshold and the 20-day moving average. The selloff was concentrated in large-cap index heavyweights: TSMC (2330) fell ~2% below its monthly moving average, MediaTek (2454) and Delta Electronics (2308) dropped over 9%, Yageo (2327) shed more than 8%, and HonHai (2317) declined over 3%.

A key driver of the correction is the unwinding of retail investor "FOMO" (Fear of Missing Out) positioning that had accumulated during a 16,000-point rally since April. Margin financing balances surged from NT$385.9 billion in early April to NT$611 billion by June 25, a warning sign of excessive leverage. Over 1,600 listed companies declined on the day.

Foreign investors accelerated capital outflows, using blue-chip stocks as liquidity vehicles. Institutional analysts note a fundamental "information vacuum" exists until mid-July as Q2 earnings season has not yet begun, leaving the market without positive catalysts. The advice from First Capital Investment Advisory Chairman Huang Yi-ting: stay disciplined, avoid chasing, and wait for a confirmed bottom before selectively re-entering quality names. **Market implication:** Near-term index upside is constrained; foreign selling pressure and elevated retail leverage suggest volatility risk remains elevated. Investors should monitor foreign investor flow data and margin balance trends closely.

---

medium.title: U.S. Markets Close Mixed: Micron Drives Semiconductor Surge but Apple Price Hikes Drag Nasdaq to Fourth Straight Loss
medium.summary:
U.S. equities closed mixed on Thursday as a blowout Micron earnings report drove broad semiconductor gains — with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index surging 3.6% toward its best quarterly performance on record — but Apple's announcement of Mac and iPad price hikes weighed on tech sentiment, pushing the Nasdaq to a fourth consecutive decline, its longest losing streak since March. TSMC's ADR fell 1.3%. May PCE inflation rose to 4.1% year-on-year, breaching the 4% threshold for the first time in three years, driven by energy costs and AI infrastructure spending, though core PCE monthly gain of 0.3% was in line with expectations. Micron surged 15.7%, citing a fourfold revenue increase and forecasting chip shortages extending beyond 2027, with 16 long-term supply agreements signed with customers.

**Relevance:** TSMC ADR weakness and elevated PCE inflation have direct implications for Taiwan export demand and CBC monetary policy considerations. The semiconductor supply tightness narrative reinforces a constructive medium-term outlook for Taiwan's chip sector.

medium.title: Evergreen Marine Vessel "Ever Lovely" Attacked in Strait of Hormuz; IMO Suspends Evacuation Plan, Adding Risk to US-Iran Ceasefire
medium.summary:
The IMO suspended its vessel evacuation plan for ships stranded in the Strait of Hormuz after a Singapore-flagged vessel — identified as Evergreen Marine's (2603) "Ever Lovely" — was struck by an unidentified projectile near the Omani coast on Thursday, with no casualties reported. A U.S. official attributed the attack to Iran's military. The incident complicates a recently signed temporary US-Iran agreement to reopen the Strait and extend the ceasefire by 60 days. The Ever Lovely, with a capacity of 8,508 TEUs and a deadweight of approximately 104,000 tonnes, is operated by Evergreen Marine Singapore.

**Relevance:** A direct operational risk event for Evergreen Marine (2603). Prolonged Hormuz disruption could affect freight rates, vessel routing costs, and insurance premiums. Investors in Taiwan shipping stocks should monitor ceasefire negotiations and any damage assessment updates from Evergreen.

medium.title: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang: Physical AI is the Next Wave of Growth
medium.summary: At NVIDIA's shareholder meeting on June 24, CEO Jensen Huang declared that the company has entered a new era of AI infrastructure, describing it as a "pivotal growth phase." He emphasized that physical AI — encompassing robotics, autonomous vehicles, and smart factories — represents NVIDIA's next major growth frontier. Huang also addressed AI ROI concerns, arguing that NVIDIA's systems deliver the lowest cost-per-token and highest throughput, justifying continued enterprise investment. Notably, he warned that any attempt to smuggle NVIDIA chips or systems into export-controlled markets such as China would face significant operational challenges, as NVIDIA will not provide support or maintenance for such goods. For Taiwan-focused investors, NVIDIA's sustained infrastructure expansion narrative directly underpins continued demand for TSMC's leading-edge nodes and reinforces the long-term AI capex cycle benefiting Taiwan's broader tech supply chain.

medium.title: Micron's Blowout Earnings Lift Taiwan PCB Suppliers Taiwan Surface Mounting and Tripod Technology
medium.summary: Memory giant Micron delivered standout quarterly results, guiding that it sees "no point in time where supply catches up with demand," reinforcing a sustained memory upcycle. Institutional investors expect the positive read-through to extend to Taiwan memory players Nanya Tech and Winbond, as well as PCB manufacturers. Tripod Technology reported May consolidated revenue of NT$8.654 billion — a consecutive monthly record high, up 5.5% MoM and 46.6% YoY — with strong order visibility extending into H2. Taiwan Surface Mounting (6278), a key DDR5/DRAM module SMT/PCBA supplier, is targeting 5–10% full-year revenue growth in 2026, adding ten production lines to meet customer demand. The combination of AI server PCB demand overflow and rising memory module board pricing (partly reflecting gold price pass-through) is driving order momentum well above prior market expectations.

medium.title: AI Wave Drives North America Air Cargo Rate Hike in July
medium.summary: Taiwan's air cargo rates for North America-bound exports are set to rise again in July, with logistics operators indicating prices will increase from approximately NT$300/kg to NT$320–350/kg. Despite a decline in fuel surcharges following lower global oil prices, overall air freight rates continue to climb — a dynamic attributed to surging AI-related cargo demand. Beneficiaries include China Airlines (2610), EVA Air, Starlux Airlines, and logistics firms including Dimerco, Dimerco Express, Tasco, and Taiwan Air Cargo. Yuanfa Port's "Yuanfa Aviation Free Trade Zone," Taiwan's only air-port free trade zone, has also emerged as an AI chip industry cluster and is expected to post record operating performance this year. The trend underscores AI hardware shipment volumes as a structural driver for Taiwan's logistics sector through at least Q4 2026.

medium.title: Foreign Investors Net Sell NT$250 Billion in Taiwan Equities Over Three Days; Institutional Players Expect Rally to 50,000 After Quarter-End Rebalancing
medium.summary: Foreign investors continued to reduce Taiwan equity exposure for a third consecutive session, accumulating net sales of NT$256.5 billion over the three-day period, following a single-day record sell-off of NT$177.4 billion the prior session. On June 25, net foreign selling moderated to NT$40.51 billion, with TAIEX futures net short positions declining by 2,554 contracts — though outstanding net shorts remain at 81,051 contracts, the second-highest on record. Despite the heavy institutional selling, the TAIEX rebounded 211 points (+0.4%) to close at 46,255, supported by Micron's better-than-expected earnings results reducing AI demand concerns and intervention from government-backed funds (eight major state-owned banks collectively bought NT$70.8 billion over three days). Institutional analysts broadly attribute the selloff to quarter-end portfolio rebalancing rather than a structural shift in outlook, and expect the index to resume its advance toward the 50,000-point level once rebalancing is complete. Domestic margin balances remain elevated, suggesting near-term volatility risk persists.

medium.title: Shin Kong Mitsukoshi Confirms Tainan Zhongshan Store Closure in October; Site Rumored for Major Redevelopment
medium.summary:
Shin Kong Mitsukoshi officially announced the closure of its Tainan Zhongshan store — one of Taiwan's longest-running department stores, having operated for nearly 30 years since 1996 — at the end of October 2026, following the expiration of its lease agreement. The company stated that Tainan consumers will be served by its Tainan Xintiandi and newly opened Tainan Xiaobei Men locations going forward. Market sources indicate the Zhongshan site is slated for substantial redevelopment: lower floors are reportedly planned for conversion into an open-format lifestyle complex (potentially operated by the Taimall shopping center team), while upper floors (9F–13F) are rumored to be earmarked for an international hotel brand. This strategic retreat from a legacy location reflects ongoing structural pressure on Taiwan's traditional department store model and a broader industry pivot toward mixed-use, experience-oriented retail formats — a trend relevant for investors tracking Taiwan's retail real estate and commercial property sectors.

---

medium.title: Taiwan Stock Market Opens Sharply Lower — TSMC Breaks Monthly MA, Index Drops Nearly 740 Points; Who Is Holding Up?
medium.summary: Taiwan's weighted index opened down 66.66 points on June 26 before accelerating lower as TSMC (2330) broke its monthly moving average at the open, dragging co-heavyweights MediaTek (2454), Delta Electronics (2308), UMC (2303), and Hon Hai (2317) lower — the index fell nearly 740 points intraday, breaching the 46,000-point level and the 10-day moving average. While U.S. semiconductor stocks were lifted by Micron's strong earnings (Micron +15.74%, Philadelphia Semiconductor Index +3.59%), Apple's 6%+ decline weighed on the Nasdaq, which closed down 0.46% for a fourth consecutive session. TSMC ADR fell 1.32%. The substrate/PCB sub-sector (ASE, Nan Ya PCB, Boardtek, Unimicron, Zhen Ding) showed relative resilience. The divergence between strong U.S. memory/AI sentiment and Taiwan's broader market weakness underscores the fragility of sentiment at elevated index levels.

medium.title: MediaTek (2454) Breaks Below NT$4,000 Amid Broad Market Correction Despite Positive Long-Term Outlook
medium.summary: MediaTek (2454) fell below the psychologically significant NT$4,000 level during morning trade on June 26, swept lower by the broad market correction despite a constructive fundamental outlook. The company's Q2 revenue guidance (based on USD/TWD at 31.5) is NT$140.2–149.2 billion, implying a QoQ decline of 6% to flat and YoY decline of 7% to 1%. Cumulative January–May revenue was NT$243.321 billion, down 1.5% YoY. However, several positive catalysts support the medium-term view: MediaTek's CPU collaboration with Nvidia on the RTX Spark "super chip" for Windows on Arm PCs; progress on its AI accelerator ASIC project for a major U.S. hyperscaler CSP, expected to enter mass production on schedule; and management's projection of approximately USD$2 billion in AI ASIC revenue in Q4 2025, with overall USD revenue guided to grow mid-to-high single digits YoY. The NT$4,000 breakdown is technically notable but may represent an entry opportunity for investors with a medium-term horizon focused on the AI ASIC and Arm PC themes.

medium.title: U.S. May PCE In Line with Expectations — Taiwan Index Futures Night Session Turns Positive
medium.summary: U.S. May core PCE came in at 3.4% YoY, in line with market expectations. Taiwan index futures (night session) initially opened lower at 46,430 on June 25 before recovering to 46,740 (up 213 points, +0.4%), with an intraday high of 46,884. Analysts noted Micron's strong earnings helped lift AI and memory-related sentiment, but cautioned that the Taiwan market's significant prior gains and heavy overhead supply — particularly from foreign and short-term investors unwinding at elevated levels — mean the correction may not yet be complete. The monthly moving average is identified as the critical near-term support and observation level; a stable consolidation near that level with declining volume would suggest selling pressure is being absorbed, while a failure to hold the monthly MA would imply the correction is ongoing.

medium.title: SCFI Freight Rate Index Rises for Nine Consecutive Weeks; US West Coast Rates Surge 11% — Taiwan Container Shipping Trio Set for Strong Q3
medium.summary:
The latest Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI) rose for the ninth consecutive week, reaching 3,239.64 points — up 3.8% week-on-week — with all four major shipping lanes posting gains. Far East to US West Coast rates climbed 11.4% to USD 6,067 per FEU, while US East Coast rates rose 8.9% to USD 7,484 per FEU. Carriers are planning a further general rate increase (GRI) of approximately USD 1,500 per FEU effective July 1. Taiwan's three major container shipping companies — Evergreen (2603), Yang Ming (2609), and Wan Hai (2615) — are expected to benefit from continued strong North American demand driven by peak season restocking. This sustained freight rate momentum supports a positive Q3 revenue outlook for all three names and reinforces the bullish case for Taiwan-listed shipping stocks in the near term.

---

medium.title: Taiwan Stock Market Breaks Monthly Moving Average — ABF Substrate Quartet Holds Relatively Firm; Nan Teh (南電) Hits All-Time High
medium.summary: Despite the TAIEX plunging over 1,000 points intraday and losing approximately 2,700 points over just four sessions, ABF substrate stocks demonstrated relative resilience. Nan Teh Electronics (8046) briefly hit limit-up at NT$1,145, marking a second consecutive limit-up session and setting a new all-time high, though it later pared gains to +7%. Foreign institutional analysis indicates the ABF substrate supply-demand gap will widen from approximately 4% in 2026 to 10% in 2027 and 16% in 2028, supporting continued price increases — with high single-digit price hikes expected in Q2 2026 and double-digit increases anticipated in Q3. Additionally, the expansion of agentic AI architectures is driving demand beyond AI servers into general-purpose servers, broadening the substrate demand base. **Relevance:** For fund managers, ABF substrate names (Nan Teh, Jing Shuo, Xinxing) represent a potential defensive pocket within the broader tech selloff, underpinned by multi-year structural supply shortfalls.

medium.title: Micron Surges 16% but Cannot Shield Asian Equities — Memory Sector Reverses from Green to Red; Macronix (旺宏) Outperforms
medium.summary: Micron's strong earnings beat — with management guiding for AI-driven memory supply shortages extending beyond 2027 and announcing 16 long-term supply agreements — initially lifted Taiwan's memory sector. However, broader macro headwinds overwhelmed the positive read-through: Apple announced price increases on MacBooks and iPads, Microsoft raised Xbox prices, and concerns over the Fed's policy trajectory intensified. The Nasdaq closed lower for a fourth consecutive session, South Korea's KOSPI triggered a circuit breaker with an intraday drop exceeding 8%, and the Nikkei fell over 4.5%. Taiwan's memory names reversed from gains to losses, with only Macronix (2337) managing to close in positive territory. **Relevance:** While Micron's AI memory demand outlook remains constructive for the medium term, the current macro environment and foreign selling pressure are overriding sector-specific positives in the near term.
